identity.title: MetaLA: Unified Optimal Linear Approximation to Softmax Attention Map

problem.claim: Determine the best linear approximation to softmax attention for Transformer structures.

gap.claim: The optimal design of linear attention models remains unresolved, and existing models do not satisfy all three proposed optimality conditions.

contributions.claim: Unifies existing linear-complexity models as a linear attention form.
Identifies dynamic memory, static approximation, and least-parameter approximation as conditions for optimal linear attention design.
Proposes Meta Linear Attention (MetaLA), described as satisfying all three conditions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish MetaLA as a linear attention solution designed to satisfy the three identified conditions, unlike the current linear models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that none of the current linear models meet all three conditions and characterize them as suboptimal.
The authors report that experiments on MQAR, language modeling, image classification, and the LRA benchmark show MetaLA is more effective than existing linear models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Linear-complexity alternatives have been proposed to replace softmax attention.
The optimal design of these models is stated to remain unresolved.
The work unifies existing models and specifies three conditions for optimal linear attention.
MetaLA is proposed to satisfy the conditions, with reported advantages across four evaluation settings.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a unified model form to explicit design conditions, then evaluates the proposed method across task and benchmark types.

lessons.interpretation: This alignment makes it easier to trace how theoretical criteria motivate a method and where its reported comparisons apply.
lessons.application: State design criteria before introducing a method, and map each evaluation setting to the claimed scope of those criteria.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the work has no formal design criteria or when evaluation settings cannot meaningfully test them.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify MetaLA's architecture, how each condition is formally defined or verified, baseline identities, quantitative results, or experimental protocols.
The reported comparative advantage is not quantified, and the scope or meaning of “more effective” is unspecified.
